literal: yes and no (not idiomatic, translates directly)
usage: Used to express ambivalence, partial agreement, or a mixed situation when answering a yes or no question. It is understood universally across Morocco in both casual and formal contexts. In the eastern regions like Oujda, people might say wah w la instead.

variants.label: Casual alternative
variants.note: Uses ah instead of iyyeh for yes, which is very common in everyday speech.

variants.label: Eastern regional
variants.note: Uses wah for yes, typical of Oujda and the eastern region.

variants.label: More descriptive
variants.english: a little yes and a little no
variants.note: Used when you want to emphasize that your feelings or the situation are truly mixed.

examples.arabic: واش عجبك الفيلم؟ إييه و لا.
examples.english: Did you like the movie? Yes and no.

examples.arabic: واش غادي تمشي معانا؟ إييه و لا، مازال ما عرفت.
examples.transliteration: wesh ghadi tmshi m3ana? iyyeh w la, mazal ma 3reft.
examples.english: Are you going with us? Yes and no, I don't know yet.

examples.arabic: الخدمة جديدة مزيانة؟ إييه و لا، فيها تمارة.
examples.transliteration: l-khedma jdida mzyana? iyyeh w la, fiha tmara.
examples.english: Is the new job good? Yes and no, it has a lot of hard work.
